readings.read_as: one block per (encoder, window part); every list is per body, index 0 = body 1; encoder_step is the model step the encoder's weights are from, trainer_labels the window part's first and last sample labels, observer_steps the matched observer model steps (where every sample matched); curve.values[i] is the score at penalty LAMS[i] (declaration choices.penalty_grid)

rule.score: curve_best: body 1's best world-posture content score over the penalty grid lam = 0 and lam = 200 x 4^k, k = -24 ... 2, solved in float64 by SVD on posture_content's own folds (gated: equal to posture_content's own algorithm run in float64 at all 11 shared penalties within 5.0e-4; its difference from production's float32 posture_content recorded per penalty, not gated)
comparisons: end:model against start:snapshot, the frozen encoder of model step 481,100 (later = end)
rule.paired_parts: every 300-sample part of every saved window (4 per window), read by both encoders on the same unchanged rows; a part sharing more than half its samples (by trainer label) with a part listed before it is left out: on the registered run the end window's first part (about 265 of its 300 samples inside the start window's last part), so 7 parts are expected
rule.later_lower: the later encoder reads lower on at least n - 1 of the n paired parts AND mean + t(0.975, n - 1) x SD / sqrt(n) of the paired differences (later minus earlier) is below 0 (n = 7: t = 2.447)
rule.later_higher: the later encoder reads higher on at least n - 1 of the n paired parts AND mean - t(0.975, n - 1) x SD / sqrt(n) is above 0
rule.within_spread: neither: the paired difference lies within its spread across parts
rule.unreadable: a comparison reads UNREADABLE (not a comparison) when, on any part it rules on, either encoder's curve best still sits at a grid end (lam = 0 or 3,200): that best is a bound, not a peak
rule.per_window: the rule is also read on each saved window alone (its 4 parts, none left out): the start window's rows, which both the start and end encoders trained on, and the end window's rows, which only the end encoder trained on; the pooled reading above is the rule's answer, the per-window readings show whether the difference lives in one window
rule.beside: the same counts and bounds on production's fixed-penalty gauges content and content_gain_matched, deciding nothing

scores.content_score: 1 - squared reconstruction error / squared error of always predicting the target's mean, for a ridge decoder (a linear map from the decoder's input numbers to the target numbers, fitted on 9 of 10 time blocks with 10 samples removed each side, scored on the withheld block; proprio_token.posture_content). 0 = no better than the mean, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse than the mean; not a percentage of information
scores.penalty: lam: the decoder minimises squared error + lam x the sum of its squared weights, in the input's units
scores.curve_best: PRIMARY: the highest content score over lam = 0 and lam = 200 x 4^k, k = -24 ... 2, solved in float64 by SVD on posture_content's own folds (FoldSolver); a token scaled by c scores at lam what the unscaled token scores at lam / c^2, so the best keeps its height under a pure gain (to the grid's resolution: a factor 4 in lam = a factor 2 in scale); best_at_end 'low' (best at lam = 0) or 'high' (best at 3,200) = the best is a bound at the grid's end, not the peak
scores.agreement: two parts at all 11 shared penalties lam = 200 x 4^k, k = -8 ... 2, on every run's own readings and in a planted case: (a) THE GATE: the float64 solve equals posture_content's own algorithm run in float64 on the same rows within AGREE_TOL (5.0e-4); (b) RECORDED, NOT GATED: its difference from production's float32 posture_content per penalty, the 0.0030518 point labelled 'production's float32 Cholesky rounding'
scores.content: production's gauge, fixed penalty 200: rises and falls with the token's movement size
scores.content_gain_matched: production's gauge, penalty 200 x gain^2, gain = this ratio / the repair's start ratio: fixed penalty at the reference response, the posture carried by the token's largest movements
scores.content_control: production's single control: the same tokens paired with the posture of samples half the part away (circular shift), at penalty 200; one draw, not the null
scores.null: NULL_SHIFTS circular shifts of the tokens against the target (1/10 ... 9/10 of the span), each scored on the same curve; `above` = how many of the 9 null bests the real best exceeds
scores.ceiling: the same curve with the decoder reading the input rows (raw: the 312 numbers; posture_fields: the 182 posture numbers) instead of the token: how decodable the target is from the input itself
scores.ratio: the token's standard deviation over time per number (mean over 192 numbers) / the posture's (mean over its numbers): a response scale; it certifies no posture information either way
scores.changed_input: CHANGED INPUT (production's posture-only rows: velocity and capacity held at their window mean): the response and ratio on those rows; never used by a score
scores.gain_matching_note: A pure gain (the token scaled by c) leaves content_gain_matched unchanged and moves content, since a token scaled by c scores at penalty lam what the unscaled token scores at lam / c^2. Neither fixed-penalty gauge separates the information in the token from the size of its movement; the curve's best (curve_best) does, to the grid's resolution, and is the primary reading of information held.

targets.world_posture: the repair's posture: fields 0-6 of the 26 rows (world quaternion, left-wrist-relative world-axis position / 200 cm); a whole-body turn changes it
targets.articulated: 87 hinge angles (radians; every robot: hinge but the 6 eye joints) from the recorded qpos at the matched observer model step; a whole-body turn cannot change them
targets.articulated_row_bodies: the 46 of those angles whose child body is one of the 26 rows' bodies
targets.groups: the 87 angles by joint group: trunk (8), head (3), arms (8), hands_and_fingers (50), legs (14), toes (4)
targets.orientation: the root body's (hip's) world rotation matrix, 9 numbers, by forward kinematics: the whole-body orientation
targets.movement_degrees: for angle targets: the angles' standard deviation over the span, mean over the target's joints, in degrees; for orientation: the root-mean-square angle between each sample's root rotation and the span's chordal mean rotation, in degrees
